significance.justification: A verified-true result would license the conclusion that agent-attributed beliefs occupy partially separable directions whose "high alignment (entanglement)" with factual-veracity directions predicts and causally produces egocentric false-belief errors; this is chiefly a form-(ii) separable-direction/causal-repair claim, with a limited form-(iii) predictive coupling between subspace alignment and error. It establishes both a behavioral phenomenon and a mechanism, fixing the expectation that steering the attributed-belief component changes "what does A think?" while leaving "what is true?" stable; this would help distinguish representational entanglement from other explanations of the inconsistent belief tracking measured by FANToM (Kim et al., 2023) and Strachan et al. (2024). True and false are determinate: a negative result would rule out alignment between self- and other-belief geometry as the proposed general explanation, although it would not rule out nonlinear representations or other mechanisms. Topic-substitution check: the generic LLM-belief topic would not earn this score; the extra value comes specifically from attributing beliefs to agents and coupling alignment to errors, but the overall shape remains the topic-median direction-plus-causal-steering template.

reach.justification: The claim hands over three named handles: "principal-angle separation" as a diagnostic, an "attributed-belief direction" for steering, and an "attribution-disentanglement regularizer" as a training-time intervention. The regularizer is ex ante because it acts before future false-belief answers, while the alignment diagnostic can forecast an error from query-time activations; both provide more lead time than merely explaining an answer after it occurs. Individual directions require re-extraction, but the asserted relation—greater self/other subspace alignment predicts more egocentric errors—would still predict what researchers should find after recalibration across the stated open-weight model families, and the regularizer could be used by model builders rather than only belief-interpretability researchers. Topic-substitution check: belief research alone supplies none of these handles, so the reach derives from the claim, although its uncertain survival across architectures and training regimes keeps it below broad deployment-level reach.
